plugins.name: afc-lite
plugins.title: AFC Lite (Automated Filament Changer)
plugins.description: Lightweight Automated Filament Changer support for the Snapmaker U1's four toolheads. Ships the AFC, AFC_unit and AFC_lane Klipper extras plus an afc.cfg that maps the four lanes (E0-E3) to the U1 extruders and filament motion sensors, and adds gcode macros for color, material, vendor, map, spool id, weight, tool change and lane/tool unload. Per-lane state feeds the U1's SET_PRINT_FILAMENT_CONFIG so the slicer and screen track what is loaded.
plugins.tagline: Four-lane filament tracking and tool-change macros for the U1.

config.label: Filament to tools mapper
config.hint: Off by default. On, a print started from the web interface or the slicer never starts until Fluidd or Mainsail has asked which lane feeds each tool, so a print sent straight from the slicer can be mapped without the printer's screen. It waits as long as it takes, and dismissing the question drops the print instead of starting it.

config.label: Filament auto loaders
config.hint: Off by default. On, once you have said which lane feeds each tool, the printer loads filament into the lanes that print needs and have none, the same way it does for a print started from its own screen, instead of starting and stopping on a filament error. It only acts on a print it held for the question above, and it leaves a lane alone when there is no spool in its feeder.

migration.summary: AFC Lite now needs a spool reader working alongside it, so this update also puts the RFID Spool Reader on your printer. What each lane already holds is kept.

plugins.name: bespok3d-daemon
plugins.title: Bespok3d daemon
plugins.description: The on-printer daemon for the Bespok3d plugin manager: a small FastAPI service that installs, updates, and removes plugins, reports printer capabilities, refuses any operation mid-print, and self-heals a plugin that breaks a service so the printer is never left unusable. It is plugin zero: the adapter bootstraps it over SSH at enrollment (cert-pinned HTTPS, bearer-token auth), not through the normal plugin install pipeline, so the install block below is intentionally empty. This package is the publishable, versioned artifact the app reads to know when a newer daemon is available.
plugins.tagline: The on-printer service that installs plugins and keeps the printer safe.

plugins.name: bespok3d-jinni-snapmaker-u1
plugins.title: Snapmaker U1 jinni
plugins.description: The Snapmaker U1's jinni: the printer-side process that reads this device's board, service and module facts and actuates the daemon's install operations on it. Bundles the shared klipper jinni runtime it extends, so a printer needs only this one package. It is not independently startable: the daemon owns its lifecycle and picks up a new jinni on the restart its own install op already performs.
plugins.tagline: The printer-side process that gives the daemon Snapmaker U1 device knowledge.

plugins.name: camera-hw-accel
plugins.title: Camera HW Accel
plugins.description:
Tap into the SoC's video pipeline instead of CPU-encoding every frame. MJPEG over HTTP at /webcam, WebRTC at /webrtc; works on any browser, smooth 30fps even with two cameras attached.

To have these auto-registered as cameras in Fluidd and Mainsail (so you don't have to add them by hand under Settings → Cameras), also install [webcam-builtin](b3d://bespok3d/webcam-builtin) for the built-in MIPI camera and [webcam-usb](b3d://bespok3d/webcam-usb) for the external USB camera.
plugins.tagline: HW-accelerated MJPEG and WebRTC streaming for MIPI & USB cameras.

# Attributions - camera-hw-accel

**Plugin author:** Bespok3d, vendoring v4l2-mpp (paxx12), Rockchip MPP, libdatachannel (Paul-Louis Ageneau) and live555 (Live Networks); two helper programs come from the Extended Firmware camera overlay `60-app-camera` (paxx12)

Hardware-accelerated camera capture and streaming.

| Upstream project | Author | Licence | Needed at runtime | Code ships in this package |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| v4l2-mpp | paxx12 | GPL-3.0-or-later | yes | yes |
| Rockchip MPP (Media Process Platform) | Rockchip | Apache-2.0 | yes | no |
| libdatachannel (WebRTC) | Paul-Louis Ageneau and contributors | MPL-2.0 | yes | no |
| live555 streaming media (RTSP) | Live Networks, Inc. | LGPL-2.1 | yes | no |

The capture and streaming binaries are built from a fork of https://github.com/paxx12/v4l2-mpp at
pinned commit `10fc3b9d935d9c79bacc014839c05de4a004c4ac`; that tree lives in this repo under
`src/v4l2-mpp/` and carries its own LICENSE. The web pages in `plugin/files/html/` and the two Python
programs `camera-stream.py` and `control-v4l2.py` are byte-identical copies from that same tree.
Rockchip MPP, libdatachannel and live555 are pulled and linked at build time by the toolchain.

Two smaller programs come from somewhere else: `fake-service` and `libv4l2-imposter.so` are derived
from the `apps/fake-service` and `apps/v4l2-imposter` sources in the Extended Firmware overlay
`60-app-camera`, GPL-3.0, written by paxx12. They live here under `src/fake-service/` and
`src/v4l2-imposter/` and differ from the overlay's originals only in identifier naming.

That overlay was called `12-camera-v4l2-mpp` until it was renamed in March 2026, and other Extended
Firmware contributors have commits in it. One of them made `fake-service` build under a cross
compiler, and that change is in the Makefile shipped here. @justinh-rahb added the V4L2 controls
integration and liberodark corrected a shebang; both of those touched the overlay's own firmware
wiring, which this plugin does not ship, because it places its own init scripts through the Bespok3d
daemon. The Extended Firmware history names every one of them.

## Copyright notices

The capture and streaming binaries this plugin ships are linked against Rockchip MPP, libdatachannel
and live555. Their licences require the notices to travel with the shipped binaries, even though no
source from those three projects is in this repo. The full licence texts are in `LICENSES/` at the
root of this repo.

| --- | --- | --- |
| v4l2-mpp fork | GPL-3.0-or-later | the project's `LICENSE` names no copyright holder line; the fork is paxx12's |
| Rockchip MPP | Apache-2.0 | `Copyright 2015 Rockchip Electronics Co. LTD` |
| libdatachannel | MPL-2.0 | the project's `LICENSE` is the MPL-2.0 text with no copyright line, which MPL-2.0 does not require |
| live555 | LGPL-2.1 | `Copyright (c) 1996-2026 Live Networks, Inc.  All rights reserved.` |

Read from `inc/rk_mpi.h` at MPP commit `437bfbeb9567cca9cd9080e3f6954aa9d6a94f18`, from `LICENSE` at
libdatachannel commit `222529eb2c8ae44f96462504ae38023f62809cec`, and from a live555 source header,
all retrieved 2026-07-28. The live555 release the toolchain fetches is `live.2025.11.06.tar.gz`,
sha256 `7614fa0a293e61b24bfd715a30a1c020fb4fe5490ebb02e71b0dadb5efc1d17c`, checked by

live555 is LGPL-2.1, so a user is entitled to what is needed to relink the shipped binary against

release at the sha256 above, the build script `src/v4l2-mpp/deps/compile_livemedia.sh` with live555's
own `linux-no-std-lib` config, the v4l2-mpp source in `src/v4l2-mpp/`, and the toolchain in
`toolchain/`, all of which are public. libdatachannel is MPL-2.0, so its source is
available from the project at the commit named above.

config.label: WebRTC stream
config.hint: On by default: the Fluidd/Mainsail camera tile is registered for the WebRTC stream. Turning it off saves memory, but ONLY do so if your camera is set to the MJPEG stream, otherwise the tile goes blank.

config.label: Built-in camera resolution
config.hint: Capture resolution for the built-in (MIPI) camera. 720p uses less memory and CPU, handy on low-RAM boards. The external USB camera always uses its own native resolution.

config.label: Recycle WebRTC viewers after (minutes, 0 = off)
config.hint: 0 (recommended): a camera stays connected as long as you watch it. Set a number of minutes to periodically recycle each WebRTC viewer connection as a memory-safety backstop on a very constrained board; the tile reconnects on its own within a couple of seconds, so it no longer freezes. Dead or abandoned viewers are always cleaned up regardless of this setting.

config.label: Wake a frozen built-in camera
config.hint: Printer firmware 2.1.0 only. On that firmware the built-in camera can freeze, and it stays black until the Snapmaker app is opened. On: when the camera sends nothing for 10 seconds, the plugin asks the printer for a photo, as the app does, and the camera comes back; it asks again once a minute, up to 5 times. Off: a frozen camera stays black until the app is opened or the printer restarts.

# Attributions - moonraker-auth

**Plugin author:** Bespok3d, switching on a Moonraker option that the Extended Firmware overlay `32-feature-klipper-tweaks` (paxx12) also switches on

Turns on Moonraker's built-in authentication.

This package ships two lines of Moonraker configuration: the `[authorization]` section and the
`force_logins` option, both Moonraker's own names. The Extended Firmware overlay
`32-feature-klipper-tweaks` (paxx12), GPL-3.0, sets the same option, so those two lines read the
same in both. The authentication itself is Moonraker's.

## Why this package is licensed as Bespok3d's own work

Two configuration lines are shared with that overlay, and both are Moonraker's own option names:
`[authorization]` and `force_logins`. Anyone switching this feature on writes the same two lines,
because they are the only names Moonraker accepts. That is too little to carry authorship, so no
part of the overlay's licence attaches to this package, and this repo is AGPL-3.0-or-later like the
rest of Bespok3d's own code.

config.label: Require login
config.hint: On: the web UI asks for a login before any control. Off: local clients connect without logging in.

plugins.name: rfid-bambu
plugins.title: Bambu Filament Tag
plugins.description: Reads Bambu Lab filament spool tags (encrypted Mifare Classic) and decodes the full filament: material, colors (both of a two-color spool), diameter, weight, and nozzle/bed temperatures into the shared rfid_data.json. plugins.name: rfid-creality
plugins.title: Creality Filament Tag
plugins.description: Reads Creality CFS filament spool tags (encrypted Mifare Classic) and decodes the filament into the shared rfid_data.json: material type, filament diameter, hotend temperature range, color, net weight, and the Creality material id. Type, diameter, and temperatures are resolved from the material id using data harvested from Creality's own slicer profiles (the tag itself does not carry them). REQUIRES TWO KEYS YOU SUPPLY: Creality tags are encrypted, so you must paste the public Creality master key and payload key into this plugin's config (see the documentation for where to get them) before a tag can be decoded. Without the keys the spool is still tracked by its tag UID. Verified against a real Creality tag for material type, diameter, temperature range, and weight. Installs the RFID Spool Reader automatically. Read-only: it never writes a tag.

plugins.attributions:
# Attributions - rfid-creality

**Plugin author:** Bespok3d, tag format documented by DnG-Crafts (K2-RFID) and the Bambu Research Group

Reads Creality filament tags.

| Upstream project | Author | Licence | Needed at runtime | Code ships in this package |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RFID-Tag-Guide and the K2-RFID community schema | DnG-Crafts (K2-RFID) and the Bambu Research Group | MIT | no | no |

The AES used to derive the sector key and decrypt the payload is a clean-room implementation of the
published FIPS-197 standard (`aes_min.py`), tested against the FIPS-197 known-answer vectors. It is
not taken from any third-party crypto library.

The filament id to type/diameter/temperature table (`creality_types.py`) is generated from Creality's own published slicer profiles (CrealityOfficial/CrealityPrint), the authoritative origin for that data. It is not copied from any third-party reader project.

config.hint: The public Creality master key (derives the card key from the tag UID). You paste it; we never ship it. See the plugin documentation. Leave empty to track Creality spools by UID only (no decode).

plugins.name: rfid-elegoo
plugins.title: Elegoo Filament Tag
plugins.description: Decoder for the filament block on factory Elegoo (Centauri) spool tags: material, color, nozzle temperature range, diameter and weight, verified field by field against a real factory spool and its label, and read on a real Snapmaker U1. The factory tag is an open NFC Type 2 tag (NTAG213-style memory, no key) that the RFID Spool Reader's standard NTAG reader picks up; this plugin decodes the pages it reads. Its layout differs from ELEGOO's published byte table: fields are page-aligned and a nozzle range is present. Elegoo's tag is small and sits further out than the U1's reader reaches for a tag that small, so a spool sitting on its holder is not read: hold the tag against the centre of the holder while the filament feeds, then mount it (steps in the doc). Confirmed on one printer and one spool so far. Needs RFID Spool Reader 0.1.15 or newer. Read-only.

# Attributions - spoolman

**Plugin author:** Bespok3d (unlucio). This is a Klipper and Moonraker helper that talks to a Spoolman server; Spoolman itself is Daniel Hultgren (Donkie) and contributors, and none of its code is here

Connects the printer to a Spoolman filament server.

| Upstream project | Author | Licence | Needed at runtime | Code ships in this package |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Spoolman | Daniel Hultgren (Donkie) and contributors | AGPL-3.0 | yes | no |

Spoolman runs on your own machine or server; nothing from it ships inside this plugin. The Moonraker
proxy component here is written from scratch. Upstream: https://github.com/Donkie/Spoolman

macros.name: SET_ACTIVE_SPOOL
macros.description: Set the selected tool as the active spool.

macros.name: CLEAR_ALL_SPOOLS
macros.description: Clear the selected spool for every tool.

macros.name: DETECT_SPOOLS
macros.description: Re-detect the loaded spools. A handy reset when spool state looks wrong.

macros.name: DUMP_SPOOLS
macros.description: Print what the bridge knows about the loaded spools.

macros.name: READ_FILAMENT_ID
macros.description: Read the selected lane's spool tag, if any.

macros.name: GET_FILAMENT_ID
macros.description: Print the currently read tag for the selected lane.

macros.name: SH_BIND_CARD_UID
macros.description: Bind the tag UID currently on a lane to a Spoolman spool, so the next tap of that tag resolves to it directly.

macros.name: SH_APPLY_TAG_TO_SPOOL
macros.description: Write what the lane's tag says onto a Spoolman spool you picked, and bind the tag to it.

macros.name: SH_CONFIG
macros.description: Change mode and logging at runtime, no restart.

macros.name: SH_DEBUG
macros.description: Print the current configuration; with a SKU, show the spool it would track.

config.label: Spoolman server address
config.hint: The whole address of your Spoolman, protocol and all: a name over https, or http and a host and port.

config.label: Selection mode
config.hint: auto: RFID is the source of truth, falls back to the manual spool. manual: the manual selection drives, tags are the fallback.

config.label: Log level
config.hint: How chatty the logs are, from least to most.

config.label: Spool resolution order
config.hint: Comma-separated, first match wins. Options: spool_id (id on the tag), uid (the tag's hardware UID, bound in Spoolman), sku.

config.label: Auto-bind tag UID on SKU match
config.hint: Opt-in (off by default). When on, a spool found by SKU that has no UID yet gets the current tag's UID written onto it in Spoolman, so the next tap is a direct UID match. Off means tags are only ever bound on your explicit request (SH_BIND_CARD_UID).

config.label: How tag UIDs are stored in Spoolman
config.hint: array: a proper list, the right shape and the default. comma_separated: the same UIDs flattened into one comma-separated value, for when another app reading this field cannot handle a list. Either form is read back correctly here.

config.label: Make a spool out of a tag Spoolman does not have
config.hint: On by default. When a tag matches nothing and none of your spools came close, the spool is created in Spoolman from what the card carries and the card is bound to it. Diameter and density are not on the card, so they are copied from your own filaments of that material; if you have none of that material, nothing is created and the console says so. This also covers writing a card onto a spool you picked (SH_APPLY_TAG_TO_SPOOL).

config.label: Track spool location in Spoolman
config.hint: When on, a spool loaded on this printer gets this printer's name written to its Spoolman location, and it is cleared when the spool is unloaded -- so you can see in Spoolman which printer a spool is on.

config.label: This printer's name (Spoolman location)
config.hint: The name written as a loaded spool's location in Spoolman (e.g. unU1jr). Location tracking is inactive until a name is set.

config.label: Spoolman pick overrides a tagged lane
config.hint: When a lane has both an RFID tag and a spool picked in Spoolman, this says which one the printer believes. Off, the tag wins. On, Spoolman wins. Turn it on if your spool profiles live in Spoolman, as they do on the extended firmware.

config.label: Where the sub-type comes from
config.hint: The three places a sub-type can come from, tried in this order, first one with a value wins. sub_type: a sub_type field you added in Spoolman. variant: the variant field the extended firmware writes there. name_inferred: we read it out of the filament name, so Matte PLA Olive gives Matte. Reorder them to change which wins, remove one to stop reading it.

plugins.name: u1-base-filament-detect
plugins.title: U1 Base: filament detect
plugins.description:
Part of the U1 Base Layer. On its own it changes nothing you can see: it opens the printer's filament detection to plugins so that other plugins can use it.

What it opens:
• A plugin can register a reader for a spool tag the stock firmware does not know, so its own tags fill in the filament details instead of being ignored.
• A plugin can ask how many filament channels the printer has, and can set the filament details for one of them.

With no plugin registered, filament detection behaves exactly as it does today. Install this because a plugin you want asks for it. Under the hood it edits Klipper's own program files on the printer. Uninstalling puts the originals back, and it re-applies itself after a firmware update. Snapmaker U1 only.

plugins.name: u1-base-print-task-config
plugins.title: U1 Base: print task config
plugins.description:
Part of the U1 Base Layer. On its own it changes nothing you can see: it opens two doors in the printer's print task settings so that other plugins can use them.

What it opens:
• A plugin can ask the printer to stop resetting pressure advance at the start of a print, and to let it go again afterwards. Several plugins can ask at the same time, and the reset comes back only once the last one has let go.
• A plugin can allow FORCE=1 on SET_PRINT_PREFERENCES, so a preference can be changed while a print is running. With no plugin asking, the printer refuses mid print exactly as it does today.

Install this because a plugin you want asks for it. Under the hood it edits Klipper's own program files on the printer. Uninstalling puts the originals back, and it re-applies itself after a firmware update. Snapmaker U1 only.

collections.name: all-the-tags
collections.title: All the Tags
collections.description: Installs the whole RFID filament-tag reading stack in one click: the NFC reader and hub, every shipped tag-standard decoder, and Spoolman tracking, so almost any spool you tap is identified and tracked. Includes the open standards (OpenTag3D, OpenPrintTag, generic NDEF JSON, TigerTag) plus full payload decoders for the proprietary tags (Bambu and Creality, with your own keys pasted into their config; without a key they fall back to UID-only tracking). QIDI needs no key at all: its tags sit on the Mifare factory default key, so those spools read out of the box. Anycubic decodes SKU, color, diameter, weight and temperatures, confirmed against real tags across three product lines. Creality now decodes material type, diameter, temperature range, color and weight, verified against a real tag (the Creality decoder is a recent release candidate, so color may not yet match every spool). The members install together with a single service restart.

collections.name: materials-tracker-plus
collections.title: Materials Tracker Plus
collections.description: Know what filament is loaded, how much of it is left, and see it in the right colour on screen. Installs the whole RFID tag-reading stack (the NFC reader and hub plus every shipped tag decoder, so almost any spool you tap is identified), Spoolman tracking to keep the remaining length up to date, AFC Lite for the automated filament changer, and the U1 G-code preview colours so the sliced preview shows each tool in its real filament colour. Anycubic and Creality now decode fully against real tags (Creality via a recent release candidate, so its color may not yet match every spool); Bambu and Creality need your own keys pasted into their config, and without a key they fall back to UID-only tracking; QIDI needs no key. Everything installs together with a single service restart. Early-access (testing) channel until the stack is verified end to end on a real printer.
collections.tagline: Tap a spool, and the printer knows what it is, how much is left, and what colour it prints.
